narrative.overview:
Chronicle looks like a well-kept log: near-black slate surfaces, one-pixel hairlines, small sober type, and colour that appears only when it means something (a phase, a status, an entity kind). The interface stays out of the way of the timeline and graph, which are the content. Density is a feature; a compact table mode exists and is honoured everywhere.

Dark is the default; the values in the front matter are the dark theme, the light values sit under "Light theme" in Colors. Light is a full inversion of the same scale (every Tailwind shade swaps to its mirror), not a second palette, so hierarchy and contrast relationships survive the switch. The theme follows the operating system unless the user picks one.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first, light by scale inversion; both are first-class.
Hairline borders (white at 10 %) instead of fills or shadows to separate regions.
Sky is the single interface accent; violet appears only as the far end of the primary-action gradient and for system entities.
Phase and status colours carry data meaning and are never reused as decoration.
German copy, short labels, monospaced keys and timestamps.

rules.name: The Colour Is Data Rule
rules.body: Red, yellow, orange, green, blue and rose are reserved for phases, statuses and errors. Decorative surfaces stay slate or sky.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Sky is the only interface accent. A screen with two competing accents is wrong.

rules.name: The Mirror Rule
rules.body: Colours are written as theme variables (`--slate-900` etc.), never hard-coded dark values, so the light theme inverts automatically. Text on bright accent buttons stays `ink` (#020617) in both themes.

rules.name: The Identifier Rule
rules.body: Keys, roles and times are monospace; prose is never monospace.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Lists, tables and forms carry no shadow. If it doesn't float, it doesn't cast. On the dashboard a timeline card is flat: its phase colour is the 3px left edge, and selection is a 2px ring in that colour, not a glow.

dos: Do separate regions with a 1px hairline (white at 10 %) before reaching for a fill or shadow.
Do write every colour through the themed variables so light and dark both work.
Do use the gradient primary button once per view; everything else is secondary or ghost.
Do set keys, roles and timestamps in JetBrains Mono at 12px.

Do keep every control and button-like link at least 44px high on narrow screens and touch devices; `input.css` does this for `button`, `select`, `summary`, inputs, `a.rounded-lg` and checkbox labels, and isolated text links add `max-sm:min-h-11` themselves.
Do keep German labels short and let the table density setting apply to any new table.
Do keep phase and status colours identical across list, timeline, graph and report.
donts: Don't use red, yellow, orange, green or blue for anything but phase, status or error meaning.
Don't add a second interface accent next to sky.
Don't put shadows on lists, tables or in-page cards.
Don't add colour halos or glows to cards, buttons, dots or logos. Phase colour is an edge or a ring, never a glow.
Don't hard-code dark-theme hex values in templates; the dashboard stylesheet still does in places and should be migrated.

Don't add new external font or script requests; reports must keep opening without the network (ADR 0006). The dashboard uses Inter while the other pages fall back to the system sans; decide deliberately before extending either.
Don't remove or replace the focus outline; a colour change alone is not a focus indicator.
